s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal syndrome with vomiting and gastric distension
key_facts: Progressive inability to tolerate oral intake
Abdominal ultrasonography and plain radiographs showed marked gastric distension
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed compression of the third portion of the duodenum

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal syndrome with vomiting and gastric distension
key_facts: Progressive inability to tolerate oral intake
Abdominal ultrasonography and plain radiographs showed marked gastric distension
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed compression of the third portion of the duodenum

shortlist.label: Superior mesenteric artery syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta at an acute angle

shortlist.label: Gastric outlet obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Intractable vomiting and marked gastric distension

shortlist.label: Duodenal obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum and postprandial upper abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Gastroparesis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive inability to tolerate oral intake and marked gastric distension

shortlist.label: Duodenal stenosis
shortlist.why_kept: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum and bloating

raw.rationale: The contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta at an acute angle, which is a hallmark of superior mesenteric artery syndrome. The patient's marked leanness and compliance with a month-long religious fasting also support this diagnosis, as weight loss can exacerbate or precipitate this condition.

rejected.label: Gastric outlet obstruction
rejected.why: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy was normal, with no intrinsic luminal lesions, making an obstructing lesion at the gastric outlet less likely

rejected.label: Duodenal obstruction
rejected.why: While there is compression of the duodenum, the specific syndrome is better described by the anatomical relationship of the superior mesenteric artery to the duodenum

rejected.label: Gastroparesis
rejected.why: Gastroparesis would not explain the compression of the duodenum seen on CT, and the presence of marked gastric distension could be secondary to the duodenal compression

rejected.label: Duodenal stenosis
rejected.why: The normal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy makes a fixed stenotic lesion of the duodenum less likely, and the CT findings point more towards an extrinsic compression syndrome
